macro_regime: German fiscal-led recovery against a hawkish ECB; eurozone manufacturing inflecting up while Germany trades at a deep relative discount
thesis_summary: Long Germany vs. broad EAFE at the 17th percentile of the 52-week ratio range. The €500bn infrastructure fund plus >1%-of-GDP defense ramp is now flowing into the data — July composite PMI jumped to 51.9 with the fastest manufacturing output growth since March 2022 and Germany expanding for the first time in four months — yet EWG/EFA is still -7.2% YTD. The ratio turned up +2.0% over the past month; we are buying the confirmed inflection, not the knife.
thesis_detail: Germany is the cheapest DM recovery story on the board. EWG/EFA at 0.4055 sits at the 17th percentile of its 52-week range (0.3945–0.4778), having de-rated all year on China-export pessimism and the ECB's June hike (depo to 2.25%, first of the cycle). Three things changed in the last six weeks: (1) Fiscal flow is real, not announced — the FXStreet German fiscal tracker (Jul 27) shows infrastructure-fund borrowing and defense outlays accelerating through 2026, with €58.9bn of special-fund borrowing in the 2026 budget and record €126.7bn investment. (2) The data inflected: flash July composite 51.9 vs 50.0, manufacturing output fastest since Mar 2022, Germany back above 50 with the cleanest combination of output, new orders and export orders in the bloc — the orders-led pattern that precedes 2-3 quarters of industrial production gains. (3) Price confirmation: EWG/EFA +2.0% over the last month while the crowded periphery trades (EWI, EWP both 96th percentile) stalled. The hawkish ECB is a headwind for duration-sensitive defensives but is itself evidence the domestic demand impulse is biting; German industrials, defense names and construction-exposed names are the beneficiaries of the fiscal mix, and they dominate EWG. Structurally, we flag our own bias: this seat is prone to permanent Europe-bearishness — the discipline here is that the data, not the prior, is doing the talking. The biggest risk is the ECB over-hiking into the fiscal impulse (Sep meeting) or a renewed China leg down hitting autos/chemicals; the stop sits just below the 52-week ratio low, so a fresh low closes the trade with the thesis falsified.

base_case: Fiscal impulse keeps feeding orders and IP through Q4; ECB delivers one more hike and holds, which the market already prices. EWG/EFA mean-reverts toward the middle of its 52-week range as German earnings revisions turn positive. Ratio to ~0.426 (+5%).
bull_case: Orders-to-production handoff plus defense procurement announcements drive a full re-rate; ECB signals pause after September; China stimulus stabilizes auto exports. Ratio toward 0.44+ (upper half of range, +8-9%).
bear_case: ECB over-hikes into the impulse (hawkish September surprise) or China rolls over again, German PMIs relapse below 50 and the ratio makes a new 52-week low through 0.3954. Stop takes us out; thesis falsified by the data, not by drawdown pain.
